target_customer: Frontier AI labs and robotics companies buying real-world human task data; local data partners who run collection businesses
problem: Robot policies need diverse real-world data showing how people do physical work, which cannot be bought because it was never captured.
business_model: Data sales to AI labs; hardware and platform supplied to local data partners who are paid per qualified hour
product_category: Physical AI egocentric data network with wearable capture devices

founders.name: Tim Li
previous_startups: Talex (expert network for LLM data annotation)
founders.background_notes: YC page says he leads strategy, hardware operations, supplier networks and commercial; outcomes of earlier startups not stated.

founders.background_notes: Owns perception and the data engine per YC page.

competitors.funding_then: An $8.2M raise is mentioned in a search result title

technical_complexity.rationale: Requires custom stereo capture hardware manufactured at scale, a quality pipeline and payments across seven countries.

defensibility.rationale: A distributed partner network and data diversity are hard to copy quickly, but many vendors sell egocentric data and hardware is replicable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Established data vendors already advertise egocentric collection in 2026; no acquisition of DeepReach found.

market_need_then: Physical AI labs are data constrained; company claims several million dollars in contracts with frontier labs and robotics firms and 475 devices and 100 plus partners in 7 countries (self-reported, inconsistent figures on the YC page).

branding.domain_note: Uses deepreach.ai; a Paris adtech firm named DeepReach (founded 2017) also exists per Dealroom.

identity.voice_and_tone: Mission-driven phrasing such as anyone can run a data business.

branding.brand_signature: Anyone can run a data business
branding.community_and_virality: Founder CTO was listed as a speaker at a robotics event on Luma; no press about the brand itself found.

brand_strength.rationale: Other companies share the DeepReach name and third-party profiles mix them up, with no press or community about the brand.

outcome_analysis: DeepReach is an active Summer 2026 company claiming early commercial traction with frontier labs through a distributed partner model. The claims are self-reported and internally inconsistent, funding is not verified, and egocentric data is a crowded field, so the outcome is open.
notes: Funding unverified: Standout Work lists last stage Seed with Y Combinator and no amount; the YC page cites customer contracts, which are revenue not investment. YC page figures conflict (clips 150,000 vs 500,000, countries 50 vs 20, Talex annotators 7,000 vs 70,000). Outcome search found no acquisition, shutdown or layoffs. Competitor details come from 2026 vendor pages and search snippets, not opened pages.
